- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3+ points), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model frequently overestimates continuation; cap upward momentum at 1–2% above recent high.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., ±0.2); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for lagged sentiment influence.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the window (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days to reflect slower initial reaction.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.7 to -0.5), model fails to adjust quickly; apply a 2–5% downward correction to forecast 3–5 days ahead.
